m042_add_bookmark_thumbnail_path.sql: Initial implementation used a stored procedure to guard against missing movies_bookmarks table. The IF EXISTS guard on the table combined with ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS on the column makes the migration fully idempotent.

comments.note: Fix-Forward applied: renamed MigratesFrom40To41_AddsOriginalFilenameColumn to MigratesFrom40ToExpected_AppliesAllPendingMigrations. The old name was stale in two ways: (1) it said 'To41' but the migration now advances to ExpectedRevision (42); (2) the method applies m041+m042, not just m041. Migration SQL is clean: comment block explains the IF EXISTS rationale (fresh dev DBs may not have movies_bookmarks), inline rollback procedure is consistent with prior migration patterns, and the two-statement body (ALTER TABLE IF EXISTS + UPDATE spdb_config) exactly matches the idiomatic pattern established by m036-m041.

Sentinel literal at line 173 correctly uses 42 (not DatabaseBootstrapper.ExpectedRevision). The tripwire comment is explicit and accurate: 'Do NOT replace this literal with DatabaseBootstrapper.ExpectedRevision — that would defeat the purpose of the sentinel.' Pattern is maintained correctly.

Test coverage gap (low-priority, not a blocker): MigratesFrom40ToExpected_AppliesAllPendingMigrations verifies that migrations 40→42 succeed and that movies.original_filename (m041) is present, but does not verify movies_bookmarks.thumbnail_path (m042). A future test enhancement could conditionally verify thumbnail_path when movies_bookmarks exists.

m042 rollback note at constraints.md line 66 is excellent: it includes the fresh-dev-DB special case ('If movies_bookmarks does not exist, only the spdb_config update needs to be reversed'), which is not present in earlier rollback notes. This anticipates operator confusion and sets a good pattern for future migrations with IF EXISTS guards.
